protocol.operation: Store::update toggling one synthetic request's once_suggested flag; real Store clone, pretty JSON serialization, tempfile write, file fsync, rename and directory fsync

source_concurrency_findings.finding: Store.update clones the entire Store; save serializes all fields, writes a new file, fsyncs it, renames it and fsyncs the directory (save:124-134). Production callers such as exec.submit/finish perform this while holding the shared std::sync::Mutex. The benchmark measures update itself without lock contention.

Each dispatcher pass scans the full jobs vector and clones matching nonterminal outbound jobs; it also clones outbound_requests. Default poll interval is 2 seconds (job.rs:89-96). Normal active-ID tracking gives one attempt per ID at a time, but no fixed total attempt limit.
A task join error clears the whole active-ID set while other tasks may still exist, so one-per-ID attempt tracking is not a universal bound across task failures.

Mesh accept spawns a task per connection without a concurrency semaphore. Requests have a 64 MiB frame bound and 10-second network-stage deadlines; these are per-message/time bounds, not a total connection or memory budget.
Owner listener spawns a task per accepted Unix connection with no fixed connection cap in this baseline; owner line parsing at local.rs:87 has no line-size bound.

Each newly accepted granted invocation spawns a task/process; there is no global process limit. Capture limits are 4 MiB per output stream (exec.rs:182). The once-grant reservation constrains that grant, not the total number of other granted commands.

limitations: Single-process, uncontended Store::update calls on one local Linux machine; this is not owner CLI/RPC latency, concurrent workload throughput, two-machine operation or proof under disk exhaustion.
Five warmups and 51 measured updates per case, fixed ascending case order; warm page/allocator/filesystem caches. p95 is nearest-rank over 51 samples, not a long-run service-level estimate.

The first baseline run overlapped one rustc process at its start; its raw samples remain preserved. The baseline repeat and compact run had zero rustc processes at sampled start/end only. Other background activity, CPU scheduling and power state were not controlled.
CPU governor was powersave. No CPU affinity, dropped caches, storage-device isolation or physical power-loss test was used.

Outputs are deterministic synthetic UTF-8 test/diagnostic lines represented by Vec<u8>; repetitive text is compressible. Btrfs compression is enabled. Logical serialized bytes are measured, not physical device writes.
Files were written and fsynced through the real production Store.save path, then reopened for equality verification. Successful fsync is not an independently observed power-loss durability guarantee.

Largest baseline state was 23,106,222 bytes (below the 30 MiB hard bound); largest saved binary output corpus was 1,843,200 bytes. Larger histories/outputs and operational longevity remain unmeasured.
Clone-only and serialization-only diagnostics are separately timed with resulting-object drop excluded; they do not sum to total update latency.
Only production variant change is serde_json::to_vec_pretty(self) to serde_json::to_vec(self). Full Store clone/rewrite, retained history growth and shared-lock scope remain unchanged.
